# Specimen leaves: MANIFEST

CA-published test and specimen end-entity certificates, used by the pipeline tests (AC2, AC5).
`TestSpecimenManifest` (`internal/engine/specimens_test.go`) parses the table below and checks, for every
`committed` row, that the file holds exactly one clean PEM `CERTIFICATE` block, that the SHA-256 of
its DER equals the `sha256(DER)` column, that the issuer CN and the validity dates match, and that
Go parses it. Every `.pem` in this directory must be listed as `committed`. A `withheld (R-P1)` file
must not be in the repository.

Each file is the publisher's DER re-encoded as one PEM block (`openssl x509 -outform pem`). No
private key was kept. The 28 non-DIGITEL rows come from the research fixture manifest
(`~/.cache/cert-check/research/fixtures/MANIFEST.md`, 2026-10-30). DIGITEL, Bewor and Sectigo
come from the `public_fixtures` of research digest C (other providers; not kept in this repository).

Privacy. Every committed specimen carries an explicit test or specimen identity in the subject
(Ficticio, PRUEBAS, ESPECIMEN, ESPAÑOL JUAN, Peça de Proves; NIFs 00000000T, 99999018D, 99999999R,
99999972C, 9994999x). The SAN rfc822Name values present are CA functional mailboxes
(`soporte_tecnico_ceres@fnmt.es`, `scd@aoc.cat`, `certificado.prueba@digitelts.es`). Real-person
certificates found during the research were not saved. Ruling R30 withholds the Bewor (×2) and
Sectigo (×2) specimens because their SAN rfc822Name holds a named CA employee's e-mail address.
Their fingerprints stay pinned here and in the provider declarations. Their pipeline rows run
only under the `live` build tag, from files kept outside the repository.

Expected pipeline result: from the plan, measured on the scratch pipeline with the clock at
NotBefore+30 min.
Left of ` / `: production markers (run 1). Right: all test markers emptied (run 2). The first word
of each side is the `certcheck.ErrorCode`.
